sentence: This project studies how poison exons control genes during vertebrate development, using long read sequencing to find them and disrupting them to test their roles.
This project builds a quick method that counts Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells in patient blood using surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy and machine learning.
This project studies how a transcription factor helps set up and keep the identity and connections of nerve cells in a nematode.
This project studies how losing gene regulatory elements shaped human brain evolution and how that relates to autism and epilepsy.
This project studies how faulty production of a type of RNA changes gene expression in T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
This project builds statistical methods and computer tools that use identical-by-descent segments to find genetic links to Alzheimer's Disease and related brain imaging traits.
This project studies how a protein drives bone metastasis and how lipid metabolism helps tumor cells adapt to bone.
This project studies how the control of gene activity shapes the way T cells differentiate and form memory.
This project studies how area-level factors and individual-level socio-economic position affect cardiovascular disease outcomes in adults diagnosed with cancer.
This project builds and tests devices that help people with disorders of the brain and nervous system, such as spinal cord injury or stroke.
This project studies how stretching cell membranes creates pores, using microfluidic and optical nano-imaging technologies to look at their structure and permeability.
This project studies whether a viral protein called latent membrane protein 1 helps Epstein-Barr virus start the lytic cascade.
This project studies how breast cancer spreads to the brain and works on a stem cell-based therapy for brain metastases.
This project tests whether the proteins that regulate calcium uptake shape calcium signals, redox homeostasis and the dynamics of mitochondria.
This project supports laboratory testing that helps detect contaminated or adulterated animal feed or drugs early.
This project studies how bioactive metabolite pathways that lead to endothelial dysfunction relate to disease risk and progression in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
This project measures the effects of thousands of genetic variants linked to substance use disorders, including in regions that turn genes on and off.
This project determines the molecular structure of a calcium-permeable cation channel involved in pain perception and studies how it opens and responds to drugs.
This project looks for weak points in the chemoresistant cell states found in neuroblastoma at tumor relapse.
This project studies how inherited mutations in genes that repair DNA damage contribute to lung cancer susceptibility.
